function: Learned (EMODRL-ED3QN) selection of the LEO satellite and of the power trade-off weights that set terminal transmit powers for distributed collaborative beamforming uplink (p. 9).
system: 10 single-antenna terminals (omni or patch) form a virtual array uplinking to 110 LEO satellites; S-band 2.4 GHz; LoS channel; no RIS (pp. 4, 12).
method: Evolutionary multi-objective deep RL: dueling DQN agents with legitimate-action masking, trained with reinforcement learning in simulation to build a Pareto policy set (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Own simulator: circular-orbit LEO constellation and LoS channel with path loss exponent 2 and random phase; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurement (pp. 5, 12).
test_conditions: Trained once in one scenario (10 terminals, 110 satellites); policies tested at unavailability 0 to 0.2 and 8 to 12 terminals (p. 14, Fig. 9).
baselines: Non-learned: single-terminal non-DCB, achievable-rate greedy (ARGP). Learned: EMODRL variants with D3QN, Noisy-DQN, DDQN, PPO, TD3, SAC; ablations OOP, OLASM (pp. 12-13).
metrics: Average uplink achievable rate, total terminal energy, satellite switching frequency (Table II); IGD for Pareto convergence; bootstrap confidence bounds (pp. 13-14).
complexity: Big-O training O(Tevo*n*Titer*Nepo*Ndata*sum(N_{l-1}*N_l)) and inference O(T*sum(N_{c-1}*N_c)); no runtime or FLOPs reported (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 5: "we introduce a channel model incorporating LoS path loss alongside random phases"; custom LoS model, path loss exponent 2 (Table I, p. 12). TR 38.821 is cited only for elevation angles and noise density, not for the channel.
q2_support: p. 14: "Fig. 9(b) shows the performance of these trained policies changed with the terminal numbers." Training used 10 terminals (p. 12); Fig. 9(b) on p. 15 spans 8 to 12 terminals and Fig. 9(a) varies the unavailability probability p.
q3_support: p. 12: "Achievable Rate Greedy Policy (ARGP)" is the non-learned baseline; the learned baselines are "EMODRL-Noisy-DQN, EMODRL-DDQN" with PPO, TD3 and SAC agents; all compared on rate, energy and switching in Table II (p. 14).
q4_support: p. 12: "the time complexity of training EMODRL-ED3QN is O(Tevo" followed by the full order expression; the inference complexity O(T ...) is given on the same page (section starts p. 11).
q5_support: p. 12: "we consider 110 LEO satellites" in an own simulator (Table I); no code or data link appears anywhere in the paper, and the conclusion (p. 15) lists public LEO simulators only as future work.
notes: Area 6: the learned policy chooses the satellite (handover, above PHY) jointly with the terminal transmit-power weights (PHY power control for the DCB uplink), so it passes above_phy; single-antenna terminals are admitted for NTN works. Beam phases are assumed aligned (p. 5). q3 judgment: the learned baselines are standard DRL agents (Noisy-DQN, DDQN, PPO, TD3, SAC) wrapped in the authors' own EMODRL framework, and the OOP and OLASM ablations (Fig. 11) were not counted; reviewer should confirm that these count as standard algorithms applied to the same problem. q2 judgment: the conclusion (p. 15) lists varying terminal numbers as future work, which sits oddly with Fig. 9(b).
